reason: The two active-loop scheduling proposals preserve data layout and FP32 update order, so test them before proposals that add memory traffic. The 160-byte A stride is a bounded, smaller layout change, but cache conflicts are unproven; prior padding results changed an inactive path and showed no repeatable gain. Test the guarded one-step prefetch next: the supplied cache-line and stride evidence makes it plausible, while the prior distance-four result on the inactive path does not settle it. The two B-packing proposals are nearly the same experiment and both add 1 MiB of allocation and packing traffic, so rank them together. A-transpose fusion applies only to fallback sizes and lacks a defined consumer layout; transpose fusion repeats A conversion across column panels and adds traffic, so it has the weakest expected net benefit.
